clue.text: Sound trees for making broomsticks?

parts.note: trees whose name, said out loud, suggests the timber a witch would pick for her broomstick

explanation.surface: A woodworker asks which trees make good, sound broomsticks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' seems to mean healthy or solid timber, but it tells you to listen to the name: it sounds like 'witch elms', just right for a witch's broom.
explanation.definitionFit: The wych elm is a native European tree whose first part sounds like the name for a broom-riding sorceress.

clue.text: Altogether heavenly, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells us the word is judged by how it is pronounced

parts.note: heavenly means holy, sacred

explanation.surface: Someone describes something as completely divine, by all accounts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns HOLY into a word pronounced the same but spelt differently.
explanation.definitionFit: Wholly means completely or entirely, just as altogether does.

clue.text: For gristle, cost of farm transport about one pound

indicators.note: about here means going around another piece

parts.note: cartage is the charge for carrying goods by cart
one is the Roman numeral I
L is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A farmer pays a pound to cart some gristle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts CARTAGE around I and L.
explanation.definitionFit: Cartilage is the tough connective tissue known in meat as gristle.

clue.text: Copy consumed by awkward stubborn brute

indicators.note: awkward hints at an ungainly jumbled arrangement of the animal's letters

parts.note: a mule is the proverbially obstinate beast
consumed means ate

explanation.surface: A copy is eaten by a clumsy, obstinate animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkward' rearranges MULE (the stubborn brute) to EMUL, then ATE follows; 'by' simply puts the two side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: To emulate is to imitate someone, matching their example.

clue.text: Animal for the doctor to utilise

parts.note: MO stands for Medical Officer, an army doctor
utilise means use

explanation.surface: A lab animal is handed to the doctor for an experiment.
explanation.walkthrough: MO is a Medical Officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A mouse is a small rodent, one kind of creature.

clue.text: The end of the line for a successful putter

definitions.meaning: the weight fixed at the bottom of an angler's fishing line
a golfer who holes the ball, sinking the putt

explanation.surface: A golfer's winning putt is described as the end of the line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The end of the line' sounds like a final finish, but it is the angler's lead weight; a golfer who sinks putts is the second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: On a fishing rig, the lead weight dropped at the bottom of the tackle; on a green, one who holes a putt.

clue.text: Raids fashionable thoroughfares

parts.note: something fashionable is said to be in
roads are public thoroughfares

explanation.surface: Attacks are carried out along trendy streets.
explanation.definitionFit: Inroads are incursions or raids into enemy territory.

clue.text: As king he had a place for elephants

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
he had contracts to he'd

explanation.surface: A monarch recalls that he kept a spot for his elephants.
explanation.walkthrough: HE'D is the shortened form of 'he had'; a kheda is an enclosure in India for catching wild elephants.
explanation.definitionFit: A kheda is a stockade in South Asia into which wild elephants are driven to be captured.

clue.text: Had second thoughts on meaning of " de-popped

definitions.meaning: taken back out of pawn, pop being slang for pawning

explanation.surface: Someone reconsiders what an odd made-up word might mean.
explanation.walkthrough: To pop something is British slang for pawning it, so 'de-popped' means bought back from the pawnbroker; split RE-DEEMED and it means judged a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: Recovering a pawned item is the standard sense; split with a hyphen it also means considered over again.

clue.text: Shines one way in valleys

indicators.note: in places the first pieces inside the word for valleys

parts.note: glens are narrow valleys, especially in Scotland
one is the Roman numeral I
ST is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: Light gleams along a path through the valleys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts I and ST inside GLENS.
explanation.definitionFit: To glisten is to sparkle or gleam with reflected light.

clue.text: You know this literary chum as well as I

definitions.text: You know this literary chum as well as I

parts.words: You know this literary chum as well as I
parts.note: a friend whom both you and I know is a shared acquaintance, and also the title of a Dickens novel

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that you know this bookish pal as well as they do.
explanation.walkthrough: A friend known to both of us is a shared friend; 'literary' points to the title of Charles Dickens's last completed novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's final completed novel, whose title phrase describes a pal that two people share.

clue.text: Cattle enclosure could be a large one

indicators.note: these letters could be rearranged into something else, so the phrase signals a reshuffle

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A cattle pen might turn out to be a large one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' makes A LARGE plus I (one) into a new arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A lairage is a pen where livestock are kept on the way to market or slaughter.

clue.text: Look for liquor, Say, and find a vegetable

indicators.note: say tells us the phrase before it is to be pronounced, giving a soundalike

parts.note: to look for liquor is to seek ale

explanation.surface: Someone goes in search of a drink and finds a vegetable instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look for liquor' is SEEK ALE, and 'say' means said out loud it matches the name of the coastal vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea kale is a coastal plant of the cabbage family whose shoots are eaten.

clue.text: Sportive, as Brutus.. confessed he wasn't

definitions.meaning: in Julius Caesar Brutus tells Cassius he is not playful

explanation.surface: A playful person contrasted with the grave Roman conspirator Brutus.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's Julius Caesar, Brutus says 'I am not gamesome', telling Cassius he lacks Antony's lively spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Gamesome means frolicsome or playful, the very word Shakespeare's Brutus uses to deny that trait.

clue.text: Illegal acts of receivers

parts.note: fences are receivers of stolen goods

explanation.surface: Crimes committed by those handling stolen property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receivers' means receivers of stolen goods, not radio sets.
explanation.definitionFit: Offences are crimes, breaches of the law.

clue.text: Among those classed generally as waterside plants

definitions.note: plural phrase, but the answer works as a mass noun for such plants

indicators.note: the answer sits among the letters of the words that follow it

explanation.surface: A botanist sorts plants generally classed as growing by the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Among' tells you to look inside 'classed generally', where the letters run across the gap between the words.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedge is a grass-like plant growing in marshes and along riverbanks.

clue.text: Scattered, like Iago robbed of his trash, say?

indicators.note: say tells us the phrase before it is judged by its pronunciation

parts.words: like Iago robbed of his trash
parts.note: Iago calls his purse trash, so robbed of it he would be relieved of his purse

explanation.surface: A Shakespeare villain loses his money, scattering it.
explanation.walkthrough: In Othello, Iago says 'Who steals my purse steals trash', so losing his trash is being 'dis-pursed', which said out loud matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Dispersed means spread widely or scattered in different directions.

clue.text: General plan is to get off track, then get back into it

indicators.note: into means the turned word goes inside the other piece

parts.note: to stray is to wander off course

indicators.note: back means the second get is read from right to left

explanation.surface: Advice for a lost walker: wander off the path, then return to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the second GET into TEG, and 'into it' places that inside STRAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A strategy is an overall plan for reaching a goal.

clue.text: Rows break out when Sister loses her head

indicators.note: break out suggests escaping, but here the letters burst into a new order
losing the head means the first letter of the word is dropped

explanation.surface: A row breaks out after a nun is beheaded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses her head' drops the S of SISTER, leaving ISTER, which 'break out' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiers are rows set one above another, as in a theatre or stadium.

clue.text: Jack up here ?

parts.note: a jack who climbs to repair tall church spires works at this height

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a fellow called Jack is up here.
explanation.walkthrough: A steeplejack climbs tall structures, so this is where he would be found.
explanation.definitionFit: A church spire is the place a steeplejack climbs to work.

clue.text: Security of the colours in this stronghold

definitions.meaning: dyes that do not run are said to be fast, and that quality is their security

explanation.surface: A regiment's colours are kept safe in a fortress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'colours' looks like a regiment's flags, but it means dyes: colour that will not run is fast.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortified refuge is a fastness; dye that does not run has colour fastness.

clue.text: Women's college plants pole in London borough

indicators.note: plants means sets something down inside another piece
in marks where the planted letter goes

parts.note: Newham is a borough in east London
N stands for the north pole

explanation.surface: A college for women plants a pole in a London district.
explanation.walkthrough: Newnham is a Cambridge college that admitted only women; Newham is a borough of east London.
explanation.definitionFit: Newnham College, Cambridge, was founded for female students and remains women-only.

clue.text: Keep writing, would you say, for the flag ?

indicators.note: would you say asks us to judge the phrase by its pronunciation

parts.note: to keep writing is to pen on

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to keep writing about a banner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep writing' is PEN ON, and 'would you say' makes it match the word for a long narrow banner.
explanation.definitionFit: A pennon is a long narrow triangular banner, as flown from a lance.

clue.text: Play time (plenty of it) for a Greek hunter

parts.note: a play is divided into acts, so play gives act
an aeon is an immensely long stretch of time

explanation.surface: A drama is staged at great length about a hunter from Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: Actaeon is the hunter of Greek myth who saw Artemis bathing and was turned into a stag.
explanation.definitionFit: Actaeon is a mythological Greek huntsman torn apart by his own hounds.

clue.text: Beastly weapon for what's left of the pack

definitions.meaning: a claw of a bird of prey or animal
in card games, the cards remaining after the deal

explanation.surface: A predator's claw is all that remains of a pack of hunters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pack' looks like a pack of animals, but it is a pack of cards; the undealt stock is called the talon.
explanation.definitionFit: A claw is a raptor's chief weapon, and in cards the leftover stock after dealing carries the same name.

clue.text: Untrue Butler's satirical anagram got him this

definitions.text: Untrue Butler's satirical anagram got him this

parts.words: Untrue Butler's satirical anagram got him this
parts.note: Samuel Butler's satire Erewhon is titled with a word spelt backwards, naming a place that does not exist

explanation.surface: Samuel Butler's satirical novel, with its invented title, got him nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: Samuel Butler's satire Erewhon is named for a land that does not exist; rearrange its title and it spells the place you reach when you get nowhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Butler's imaginary land is a place that exists in no location, which is the ironic reward his satire earned.

clue.text: Smart, getting one foot in New York

indicators.note: in means those pieces go inside the abbreviation for the city

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone smart gets a foothold in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts I and FT inside NY.
explanation.definitionFit: Nifty means neat, clever or stylish.

clue.text: Famous racehorse on newspaper staff? What lunatic obfuscation!

parts.note: Eclipse was the unbeaten eighteenth-century British racehorse
working for the newspaper called The Sun

explanation.surface: A famous racehorse seems to be working at a newspaper, an absurd muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: Eclipse was an undefeated eighteenth-century racehorse, and The Sun is a British newspaper; 'lunatic' means caused by the moon, which hides the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: When the moon passes in front of the solar disc it obscures it, an obfuscation produced by the moon.

clue.text: An unusually dry one over there

indicators.note: unusually says the letters come in an unusual order

explanation.surface: An exceptionally dry one stands at a distance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' rearranges DRY and ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Yonder is an old word meaning at some distance, in that direction.

clue.text: My jolly one, fellow member of the band

parts.note: a Jolly is slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM
one is the Roman numeral I
a don is a fellow of a university college

explanation.surface: Someone introduces their cheerful bandmate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jolly' is the slang for a Royal Marine (RM), and 'band' means Achilles' troop of warriors in the Iliad, not a group of musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: The Myrmidons were the warriors Achilles led at Troy, hence a loyal follower.
